name: Polyester
editorial_article: Released in 1995 on the influential British electronic label Rephlex Records, "Polyester" is a pivotal project by the German electronic musician and producer Lisa Carbon. Operating within a landscape of early-to-mid-90s experimental electronic music, Carbon—often associated with the artist Jan Jelinek—crafted an album that famously defies rigid genre classifications, merging the structural possibilities of techno with the fluid, improvisational warmth of jazz and lounge music. The project stands as a prime example of the "electro-jazz" hybridity that characterized certain pockets of the European experimental scene during that era, characterized by loose synth work and rhythm sections that weave between club-oriented beats and atmospheric, bossa nova-inflected soundscapes. Despite being released over a year behind its original schedule, the album remains a distinct entry in the Rephlex catalog, highlighting a playful, cerebral approach to sound design that prioritized vibe and experimentation over the harder-edged sounds often associated with the label at the time. Tracks such as "Jazz Device" and "Jambient" illustrate this bridge-building, demonstrating Carbon's ability to maintain high production values while exploring the sonic textures of vintage keyboards and unconventional rhythm patterns. The album, which includes tracks like "Soft Drink" and "Corazon Loco," remains a sought-after relic for fans of 90s intelligent dance music and experimental electronic curiosities.
editorial_pitch: A defining early exploration of electro-jazz and lounge-influenced experimental techno, released on the legendary Rephlex Records in 1995.
